issues: The quoted dialogue excerpts are accurate but omit Lehi's reported words of rejoicing and fear; the narration excerpts convey those facts instead.
Scene's description treats the account as the observer's (Lehi's) view, while the previous scene depicts Nephi's first-person account; avoid implying an uninterrupted viewpoint or chronology.
“The river’s head” and “a little way off” are supported; broader framing of a continuous landscape is a visual choice, not specified.
The suggestion that Lehi gestures toward himself or the tree is an uncertain visual inference; the text only says he beckoned.
Scene is consistent with verses 17–18. Specific uncertainty: the verses give no precise positions or distance for Laman and Lemuel, as the scene notes.
Scene is consistent with verses 21–22. Specific uncertainty: the text does not specify the people's identities, clothing, or exact positions, as noted.
The scene omits that the mist was exceedingly great, a detail explicitly stated in the verse.
The scene does not identify the observer; the surrounding account establishes Lehi as the observer of the vision.
The location 'large and spacious field' is not stated in the cited verses for this event.

The verses do not specify whether those drowned or lost from view belong to the multitudes feeling their way toward the building; the scene correctly flags this as unspecified. The fountain and strange roads are described in verse 32, but the verses do not establish where they lie relative to the building or one another.
“The strange building” is supported, but its visual appearance and interior are unspecified and should remain undesigned as fact.
Lehi’s words identify the scorners as a multitude; the exact people shown pointing and their positions are not specified.
“These are the words of my father:” is exact source text, but is Nephi’s narration, not Lehi’s spoken dialogue. Keep it as a caption.
The prior scene reports separate outcomes—drowning and becoming lost—so do not visually combine them with this scene’s building episode or imply the same people are involved.
Nephi is not identified as present when Lehi exhorts Laman and Lemuel; the text says Lehi spoke 'unto us' but does not specify who was present.
